rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening question is an expression of wonder at the hypocrites’ contradiction.
rows.anchor: look at these people who claim to be believers; on the one hand

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claim faith while befriending the People of the Book, who reject Muhammad’s prophethood and message.
rows.anchor: they claim to profess faith and on the other hand, are extending ties of friendship with the People of the Book

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for their brethren indicates Jewish-origin hypocrites: they left the Jews for advantage, but retained Jewish loyalties and allied with Muslims for political and economic interests.
rows.anchor: For their own expediencies, they left the Jews but Judaism could not leave them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most hypocrites were originally Jews; only a few Ishmaelites were hypocrites, with a different kind of hypocrisy, and this group’s conduct is discussed in Sūrah al-Mumtaḥinah.
rows.anchor: most hypocrites were originally Jews, and it is their attitude which is under discussion in the previous sūrahs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies the threatened Jewish group as Banū Qurayẓah: Qaynuqāʿ had been eliminated, Banū Naḍīr’s fate is given in this sūrah, and Qurayẓah remained near Madīnah before their post-Trench destruction.
rows.anchor: I am fully satisfied that they refer to the Jews of Banū Qurayẓah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites promised Banū Qurayẓah that if they were expelled like Banū Naḍīr, they would leave with them, ignore anyone’s advice, and support them in war.
rows.anchor: the hypocrites started to assure the Banū Qurayẓah that if they, too, are driven out like the Banū Naḍīr, then they will go with them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banū Qurayẓah expected to be next and distrusted the hypocrites after their inaction for Banū Naḍīr, so the hypocrites stressed that they would even sever ties with Muhammad and the Muslims.
rows.anchor: they did not have much faith in the promises of these hypocrites. They knew that in the case of the Banū Nad īr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s declaration that they are liars carries the same oath-like emphasis as the hypocrites’ pledge; the phrase that God bears witness itself implies an oath.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has called them liars with the same oath and emphasis with which the hypocrites had assured them of their support.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse refutes the pledge point by point: the hypocrites would neither leave with Banū Qurayẓah nor help them, and any help would end in flight; this is what happened.
rows.anchor: Consequently, this is what happened exactly. No one helped them when it was needed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like Banū Naḍīr, Banū Qurayẓah had a peace treaty with Muhammad; during the Trench, Ḥuyy ibn Akhṭab induced them to break it, arguing that Quraysh and Banū Ghaṭfān could exterminate the Muslims if Qurayẓah joined them.
rows.anchor: Ḥuyy ibn Akhṭab, the famous hypocrite, induced them to violate this treaty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Trench, Muhammad besieged Qurayẓah; no one came to help, and they turned to Saʿd ibn Muʿādh to determine their fate, after which God routed them through his verdict.
rows.anchor: At that time, no one supported them. At last, they had to turn to Sa‘d ibn Mu‘ādh (rta) to decide their fate.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means every hope of assistance will end: God delivers a decisive blow, and no aid benefits those He seizes.
rows.anchor: It will be a decisive blow from God, and no help can avail those who are seized by the Almighty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites dare not support their brethren because they fear the Muslims more than God, whom they disobey openly and secretly.
rows.anchor: because they dread the Muslims more than God. They oppose and disobey God secretly as well as openly

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is irrational to fear human attackers while disregarding the true Master; violating clear directives seals the heart against obvious realities, as 63:3 says of those who believed, then disbelieved, and lost understanding.
rows.anchor: Thus, it was regarding these hypocrites that the Qur’ān at one place has remarked:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims should ignore the hypocrites’ bullying: they will not mount an open, organized attack and will remain in houses and forts, fighting only defensively from behind walls, an ineffective method used only as a last resort.
rows.anchor: They will remain confined to their houses and forts, and will try to defend themselves from behind their walls and barricades.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews repeatedly incited Quraysh and its allies but did not fight openly; when Muslims attacked, they defended from forts and were humiliated.
rows.anchor: they have always remained very cunning in inciting the Quraysh and its allies against the Muslims; however, they have never come out to fight in the open.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their divided hearts explain their inability to fight openly: their only unity is opposition to Islam, while Jewish tribes and their Quraysh and polytheist allies harbor mutual enmity; faith, by contrast, unites Muslims.
rows.anchor: Except for the opposition they have in common for Islam, their hearts have great spite and malice for one another.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their underlying problem is failure to use reason: they follow desires instead of sense, and conflicting thoughts then bring a people to ruin.
rows.anchor: instead of facing reality, assessing it seriously and facing it with determination and perseverance, they have become a slave to their desires.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns those whom the hypocrites incited: if they take a wrong step, they will meet the fate of the recent wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: if these people, after being provoked by the hypocrites, take a wrong step

rows.speaker: People
rows.claim: The commonly held view identifies the earlier people with Quraysh and the Battle of Badr: like Quraysh, the present group will be routed.
rows.anchor: People have generally taken the words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Quraysh or Banū Qaynuqāʿ could be meant, he prefers Banū Naḍīr because their expulsion was the most recent incident and a Jewish example would best warn Qurayẓah.
rows.anchor: For this reason, I am of the opinion that these words refer to the Ban ū Naḍīr.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened fate is worldly, followed by severe punishment in the Hereafter; Qurayẓah’s worldly fate was harsher than Banū Naḍīr’s, while only God knows their afterlife fate.
rows.anchor: they will meet this fate in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have to face a grievous torment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites resemble Satan: he urges a person to disobey God, then disowns him; likewise, they encourage Qurayẓah but will flee and deny responsibility when consequences arrive.
rows.anchor: Just as he allures man to disobey God, and when a person commits some sin as a result, he starts rebuking him by becoming his adviser and withdraws his support.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Badr Satan praised and encouraged Quraysh, promising assistance; 8:48 is cited as a parallel to his encouragement before he abandoned them.
rows.anchor: no one has the courage to vanquish you this day. I shall be at hand to help you, (8:48)).
